course_title: Special Topics: American Questions: Oral History: ATL Food System
subject: AMST
course_description: Seminars arranged around current issues and controversies in American culture. May be repeated as topic changes .
course_notes: (Same as HIST 285W 1 and ANT 285W 1) (This course approaches questions of sustainability and environment in Atlanta food systems. We will foreground the methodology of oral history and storytelling to explore these themes, and will build in an experiential component. As community engaged learning, the course will put students into dialogue with individuals and organizations professionally involved with Atlanta farms, markets, and community organizing. Students will gather oral histories from our collaborators, to be included in the Rose Library's "Worldbuilding" oral history collection. As a Continuing Communication course, students will gain experience creating interview questions and frameworks, conducting interviews, transcribing, and creating archival products. This course is part of a larger project (see Emory Oral History Program website) and initiates a three-course sequence. The subsequent course explores the histories of urbanization and agriculture, and the last treats forms of community formation in food systems. Students in this Spring 2027 course may take the other courses if they wish. In all three courses, students will contribute to the oral history collection.)
